content.rendered:
Another great one gone too soon: Bruce Springsteen paid tribute to Glenn Frey, one day following his death on January 18, 2016.

“Take it Easy” was actually co-written by both Glenn Frey and Jackson Browne, and both The Eagles and Browne recorded it. The Eagles version came out first–it was, in fact, the band’s first single, released in 1972 and peaking at #12 on the Hot 100.

Take It Easy
First performed: March 16, 2004 (New York City, NY)
Last performed: April 26, 2025 (West Long Branch, NJ)

© January 18, 2018

jetpack-related-posts.title: Linda Paloma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce and Patti deliver a gorgeous cover of Jackson Browne's "Linda Paloma," more delicate and soaring than the original.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mustang Sally
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Too many team-ups! "Mustang Sally" is one of those songs you just gotta play with someone else, I guess, because the list of Bruce's "Mustang Sally" guest spots is a long one.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Purple Rain
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Two days after Prince's untimely departure, Bruce and the E Street Band took the stage in purple and delivered one of their greatest covers ever.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stay
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce and Jackson Browne team up to cover "Stay" by The Zodiacs at the 1979 MUSE concerts. Along with the other tracks from that show, it's Bruce's first live appearance on record.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Across the Borderline
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: At a pair of 1990 benefit concerts, three rock icons joined their voices and instruments for a gorgeous acoustic encore of Ry Cooder's classic song.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brother John
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce joins an all-star Survival Sunday line-up to cover The Neville Brothers' "Brother John."
